notes: The season's nobility (balance/cosmetics.json frames/noble_<id>; liveops.ranks.nobility): six frames of rising splendour, each painted as a square (left) and a ring (right) on the sheet's flat navy -- top to bottom Knight (dark iron, rivets, a sword), Baron (bronze, a coronet of four pearls), Count (silver, blue enamel, fleurs-de-lis), Duke (gold, crimson, strawberry leaves), Prince (gold set with rubies and sapphires, a jewelled crown) and Emperor (gold and crimson, the imperial crown and a double-headed eagle) -- keyed off it as frames_cosmetic_a.json's are (darkkey against the sheet's own ground [8,20,31], k 38, floor 4); the EMPTY windows key clear, so a portrait drawn under a frame shows through.

frames/noble_<id>_square and _ring at this sheet's own scales, set as frames_cosmetic_a.json's were: every square's plain band 160 across (painted 244: the median of the six, measured along each window's centre lines) and every ring's 96 (painted 203: the median outer circle on the diagonals, clear of the ornaments on the axes), so the nobles' frames are the same size on a portrait as every other frame, their crowns and eagles standing outside the band. _tile is the ring whole in the wardrobe's 224x190 art box; looks/noble_<id>_ring_large the same ring at band 132 (the podium's rings), kept here rather than in looks.json because they are this sheet's crops.

Each crop is centred on its frame's own window -- a square's from its inner edges along the centre lines clear of the middle ornaments, a ring's from a circle fitted to its inner edge on the diagonals -- and masked to a polygon round its own ink, grown 3 px and kept off a neighbour's: the count's fleurs-de-lis reach within four pixels of the baron's rim and the prince's cross within two of the duke's, so the ink is labelled unclosed and every piece given to the cell its centre falls in. Written by a measuring script (fork D's scratchpad forkD/gen_frames_noble.py): its numbers, not hand-read ones.
